# Control map

This is an implemented control inventory, not a test-run report.
Review on changed standards, mechanisms, evidence or coverage. The
[registry](control-registry.json) owns these mappings; [engineering](engineering.md)
owns mandatory wording and [charter](charter.md) owns principles.

Automatic controls run in the common lane. Runtime controls act in the live system;
their tests cover only the stated cases. Manual controls require the named review
or probe. Implementation and evidence links do not assert a current execution or pass.

## Mechanisms and coverage

### C-PORTABLE — Portable regression lane (automatic)

Controller, HTTP adapter, setup and spectator regressions. Includes gameplay record validation and bounded evidence retention using synthetic observations. Passive planner/skill/supervisor composition, continuation and uncertainty are covered by real-component synthetic fixtures. Common command compiles Python, runs selected Ruff correctness diagnostics, Import Linter contracts, JavaScript syntax checks, Python tests and delayed-image viewer tests; markdown-it-py parses document links/images before contained file-target checks; diff whitespace is checked.

Owner: maintainer. Trigger: each integration checkpoint and configured CI event.
Enforcement: Common command and opt-in local hook; main also requires the observed GitHub Actions controller check (app 15368) with strict freshness under active ruleset 25346774. Local hooks remain bypassable; dated hosted/probe evidence is in Enactive migration acceptance (original public-workflow results remain historical).
Failure response: Preserve failure output, fix the cause and rerun before claiming portable acceptance.

### C-RUNTIME — Live authority and input guards (runtime)

Single-controller and gameplay-runtime dispatch, exact external planning lifecycle, HTTP trust boundary and spectator input freshness. Controller serializes each channel, persists separate gameplay/control admissions and revokes durable host tokens before retirement; native v3 checks boundary, matching frame, expiry and token at input commit. Recovery is limited to owned native interruption queries and one raw debug Space. Server validates origin/token/frame paths and separates operator recovery ingress from ordinary commands; viewer waits for matching decoded image and supported ordinary boundary or exact eligible recovery evidence. GameplayRuntime owns one exact lease, single-use external plan requests, fresh equivalent revalidation and original task/intent deadlines; receipt exceptions remain unknown. Pause cancels applicability independently of planning/native waits. Every stopped public walk freezes/Pause/revokes its entry generation and retains actual walk-local evidence/exact terminal; only explicit successful Observe then Resume releases the hold, with semantic reassessment procedural.

Owner: controller and viewer maintainer. Trigger: every relevant request, observation and image decode.
Enforcement: Implemented at runtime; regression execution is C-PORTABLE. Source references alone establish no behavioral pass.
Failure response: Reject or freeze further dispatch; expose error and reconcile by observation before explicit resume.

### C-NATIVE — Native build and real-game acceptance (manual)

Changed native/input/rendering/protocol/compiler/source-pin behavior and new support claims. Follow native acceptance probes, inspect actual game/spectator frames and record dated outcomes, environment, candidate and hashes.

Owner: integration maintainer; lead verifies evidence. Trigger: relevant native boundary change or new native release/support claim.
Enforcement: Required by S-PROTOCOL/S-DELIVERY and release review; manual, outside the portable gate. Permission readiness before ordinary campaign input also requires S-OPS's [live permission preflight](operator-permissions.md#preflight-for-every-campaign) from the actual designated player and exact entry point. Retain enabled project-layer evidence, rule decisions and live results separately. Repeated per-action review fails permission readiness even if every request is approved; resolve it before ordinary play. This is a manual activation check; prefix matching does not prove runtime loading.
Failure response: Retain failed/unknown probes, block the affected claim and repair or document the supported limit.

### C-BOUNDARY — Architectural dependency contracts (automatic)

Declared controller and server dependency boundaries, including indirect imports through harness modules. All passive gameplay modules, including supervision, must not import controller, HTTP, CLI or process/build tooling. Shared movement policy cannot depend on consumers, clock, filesystem or transport. Import Linter uses the pyproject.toml forbidden contracts: controller cannot depend on server, CLI, declared network modules or build tooling; server cannot depend on CLI/tools; CLI may compose both. Fourth forbidden contract isolates harness.movement; negative import fixtures exercise it.

Owner: harness maintainer. Trigger: common command; architecture changes require rule review.
Enforcement: Common command runs the real lint-imports executable and propagates failure; temporary source fixtures exercise allowed composition and direct/indirect forbidden imports.
Failure response: Remove reversed dependency or review the boundary and checker together before accepting changed architecture.

Evidence / implementation: [pyproject.toml](../pyproject.toml), [tools/check.py](../tools/check.py), [tests/test_devtools.py](../tests/test_devtools.py), [docs/architecture.md](../docs/architecture.md), [docs/decisions/003-development-controls.md](../docs/decisions/003-development-controls.md), [docs/acceptance/2026-10-17-bounded-skills.md](../docs/acceptance/2026-10-17-bounded-skills.md), [docs/acceptance/2026-10-17-passive-supervisor.md](../docs/acceptance/2026-10-17-passive-supervisor.md).

### C-REVIEW — Design and independent change review (manual)

Consequential designs, implementation, tests, delegation and exceptions. Lead owns design/integration and verifies returned evidence; at most two workers use separate project-local worktrees and named disjoint paths, with shared runtime serialized; fresh-context review assesses contracts, risk and maintainability before acceptance. Review new or expanded custom infrastructure across code/docs/workflow/controls against S-CODE: name the existing option, unmet gap, smallest scope, owner/cost and retirement trigger; reject unjustified duplication. Before publication, inspect explicit Git author/committer identities and all new commit messages, including co-author trailers, under S-WORK. Use repository-local Git identity configuration. Before merging a PR whose Issue completion awaits merged-main validation, read gh pr view --json closingIssuesReferences, require an empty list and re-read after removing references. Prose negation is not a parser control; use GitHub computed data, no custom keyword parser.

Owner: lead; reviewer supplies independent findings. Trigger: significant change, new boundary/guarantee/dependency or integration checkpoint.
Enforcement: Required by S-AGENT and the GitHub work/PR workflow; independent agent review is manually recorded, not an independent GitHub human approval. Hosted enforcement is recorded separately in acceptance.
Failure response: Resolve material findings or record scoped owner/reason/revisit exception; after two unsuccessful worker repairs lead takes back the work.

### C-RELEASE — Exact candidate and evidence review (manual)

Checkpoint/release scope, source provenance and validation lanes. Inspect staged diff and candidate identity, run common checks against exact candidate, review pins/open exceptions and require relevant native probes for affected claims. Git owns tracked-source identity: commit before native acceptance and use commit/tree/diff/PR; hash external artifacts instead of maintaining per-source history.

Owner: lead or releasing maintainer. Trigger: checkpoint, release or support claim.
Enforcement: Main requires a PR, the Actions-bound controller check and resolved conversations; no force-push/deletion or configured bypass. Lead still owns native/release acceptance. Zero required human approvals is an explicit single-account limit; agent review is not human approval.
Failure response: Hold the affected acceptance/release claim until failed or unexecuted required lanes are resolved or scope is explicitly reduced.

## Interpreting results

Run `.venv/bin/python tools/check.py` for the portable lane; update this map with
`.venv/bin/python tools/governance.py --write`. The latter validates before writing and
does not run gameplay. Dated executions belong in [acceptance](acceptance/2026-10-17-mvp.md)
and [work](work.md), with exact candidate, failures and unexecuted lanes.
